title: Ordered Jobs With Same-Kind Rest Days
statement:
You must finish a list of jobs in the given order. tasks[i] is the kind of the i-th job. Each day you either do the next job or take a break.

After doing a job of some kind, you must let at least space full days pass before doing another job of the same kind. Jobs of other kinds are not affected.

Days are numbered from 1. Return the number of the day on which the last job is done, using as few days as possible.

examples.why: Day 1: kind 4. Days 2–3: break. Day 4: kind 4. Day 5: kind 2. Day 6 is too soon for kind 4 again, so it is done on day 7.
Kind 1 is done on day 1, so the second kind-1 job waits until day 5, even though other jobs filled days 2 and 3.
No rest is needed, so one job per day.

hints: The order is fixed, so the only choice is how many breaks to take before each job. Take as few as the rule allows.
For each kind, remember the day it was last done. The next job of that kind can go no earlier than that day + space + 1.
Keep a running day counter. Each job happens on max(day + 1, last[kind] + space + 1).

explain.intuition:
Since the order is fixed, you never gain anything by resting longer than required: doing a job earlier only moves later jobs earlier too. So each job goes on the earliest day allowed, which is the later of two dates: the day after the previous job, and the day after its kind's rest period ends.

A hash map from kind to the day it was last done gives that second date in O(1). Do not simulate day by day: with long rest periods the day count can reach billions, but you only need to jump straight to the right day.
steps: For each job of kind k: day = day + 1.
If k is in last, set day = max(day, last[k] + space + 1).
pitfalls: Counting the rest from the previous job of any kind instead of the previous job of the same kind.
Off by one on the gap: space full days between means the next allowed day is last + space + 1.
Looping one day at a time. With space = 100 000 and many repeats this runs for billions of days.

solutions.title: Day-by-day simulation
solutions.idea: Walk through the days one at a time. On each day, do the next job if its kind has rested long enough; otherwise take a break.

solutions.title: Jump to the earliest allowed day
solutions.idea: Each job goes on max(previous day + 1, last day of its kind + space + 1). A hash map remembers the last day per kind.

followups: Jobs may now be done in any order. What changes, and which structure helps?
Return the full schedule with the break days marked.
